name: E1_exit_only
description: REF anchor. Trigger: any net loss. Level: loss-exit price x 0.97. Reset: close >= 0.95 x frozen ref high. Remembered: exit_price, ref_high (2). correction_ends_on_reset=True (inert: no component reads the correction).
hypothesis: Reference point: the verified 3% rule (identical to REF_lower3 / B_lower_3pct). Every other Family E machine is judged against it; its known failure is that the anchor is an arbitrary exit date (the -$143 VGT 2023-01 episode).

name: E2_entry_only
description: Entry-price anchor. Trigger: any net loss. Level: last losing ENTRY price x 0.97 (st.entry_price). Reset: close >= 0.95 x frozen ref high. "No other memory" read as: no correction-level memory (no failure count, no ladder, no cumulative loss); the episode remembers only the arming trade's entry price for the level and ref_high for the reset (2 quantities, same count as E1). correction_ends_on_reset=True (inert).
hypothesis: Anchoring to what the failed trade PAID removes the arbitrary exit-date dependence of E1: after a deep loss the exit is already >=3% below entry, so re-entry is immediate at the next signal (no deep-bear spacing), while small losses are as restricted as E1. Expected to fix V-bottom misses at the cost of re-opening the 2000-02 repeated-loss problem — a diagnostic for question 5, not a candidate.

name: E3_entry_count
description: First-entry ladder + rebound reset. Trigger: any net loss. Level: correction first entry x (1 - 0.03 x n_failed), n_failed = arming losses in the correction including the current one (1st failure 3%, 2nd 6%, 3rd 9%, ... below the FIRST failed entry; no clip). Reset: close >= 1.15 x episode low (lowest close since the arming exit, st.min_close — C4_rebound_15 form). Remembered: first_entry_price, n_failed, episode low (3). correction_ends_on_reset=True (deliberate: a 15% rebound from the low declares the correction over, so the ladder resets; keeping it would anchor the next correction to a stale entry).
hypothesis: One stable anchor per correction plus a failure count spaces repeated attempts down a cascade without referencing any exit price, and the rebound reset ends the correction from the LOW (reachable in deep bears, unlike frozen95) — testing whether correction-level memory plus a recovery-defined ending beats both per-trade anchors.

name: E4_cum_loss
description: Severity-scaled discount. Trigger: any net loss. Level: loss-exit price x (1 - d), d = clip(1% + |correction cum loss| / $100k, 1%, 8%); cum loss = sum of net P&L (interest included) of the correction's arming losses including the current one. Reset: close >= 0.95 x frozen ref high. Remembered: exit_price, cum_loss, ref_high (3). correction_ends_on_reset=True (deliberate: frozen95 fires only near full recovery; a finished correction's losses must not scale the next one).
hypothesis: Restriction severity should scale with the damage done: a -$143 loss gets a 1.14% discount (nearly no restriction — directly targets the VGT 2023-01 failure) while a cascade saturates at 8% (2000-02 spacing preserved). Tests whether cumulative dollars are the right memory, independent of any individual loss size.

name: E5_no_small_rearm
description: Cumulative arming threshold. Trigger: a net-loss exit arms ONLY when exit_price / streak_first_entry - 1 <= -0.02, where streak_first_entry is the entry price of the first trade of the current run of consecutive net-loss exits (set on the first loss, kept by non-arming losses, cleared by any profitable exit and by a recovery reset). Single small losses never arm. Level: loss-exit x 0.97; reset: frozen95 (both REF). Remembered: streak_first_entry, exit_price, ref_high (3). correction_ends_on_reset=True, mirrored onto streak_first_entry via a bookkeeping-only on_session_end override (subclass E5NoSmallRearm; frozen logic runs first, unchanged).
hypothesis: The restriction exists to stop cascades, and a cascade is a CUMULATIVE decline — so arm on cumulative price damage, not on any single loss. Micro-losses (financing-only, or < 2% from the streak start) stay unrestricted (fixing VGT 2023-01) while chained small losses still arm once their sum exceeds 2% (keeping 2000-02 protection). Tests whether the TRIGGER, not the discount, is the right place for loss-size memory.
